title: Exploring the anti-metastatic potential of sunitinib and novel analogs in colorectal cancer: insights into HIF-1alpha mediated metastasis.
authors: Rassouli, Fatemeh B; Matin, Maryam M; Hadizadeh, Farzin; Nejabat, Masoud; Allahverdizadeh, Hossein; Jamali, Hamidreza; Gharedaghi, Shahin; Hassanzadeh, Halimeh
one_liner_zh: 该文研究舒尼替尼及其类似物对结直肠癌转移的抑制作用，涉及HIF-1α的分子对接与动力学模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a prevalent malignancy worldwide with high mortality rate. Metastasis, the primary cause of cancer-related deaths, is attributed to various factors including tumor hypoxia. Due to the urgent demand for potent anti-metastatic agents, we aimed to determine the effects of sunitinib and novel analogs on the metastatic behavior of human CRC cells in hypoxic condition for the first time. METHODS: For in silico analyses, pathogenic targets of metastatic CRC were identified, PPI network was constructed and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis was conducted. The expression of HIF1A was evaluated in seven CRC cell lines, and computational modeling was carried out to define the interaction of sunitinib with HIF-1alpha. For in vitro studies, analogs of sunitinib were synthesized, and cells were assessed for viability, migration, invasion, MMPs activity and gene expression in hypoxic condition. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Computational analyses highlighted the importance of HIF-1alpha as a crucial mediator of metastasis in CRC. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations demonstrated favorable and stable interaction of sunitinib and three novel analogs with HIF-1alpha PAS-B domain. Volcano plots indicated upregulation of HIF1A in LoVo cells compared to six other CRC cell lines. Findings of in vitro studies revealed considerable inhibitory effects of sunitinib and analogs on LoVo cell migration and invasion in hypoxic condition. Gelatin zymography and qPCR analysis indicated decreased activity of MMP-2 and MMP-9, along with downregulation of EMT transcription factors in hypoxic condition. Current study reports promising anti-metastatic effects of sunitinib and novel analogs on CRC cells, providing foundation for further investigation to combat cancer metastasis.
abstract_zh: 引言：结直肠癌（CRC）是全球范围内一种普遍存在的恶性肿瘤，死亡率高。转移是癌症相关死亡的主要原因，其归因于包括肿瘤缺氧在内的多种因素。鉴于对抗转移药物的迫切需求，我们首次旨在确定舒尼替尼及其新型类似物在缺氧条件下对人CRC细胞转移行为的影响。方法：在计算机模拟分析中，识别了转移性CRC的致病靶点，构建了蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络，并进行了KEGG通路富集分析。在七种CRC细胞系中评估了HIF1A的表达，并通过计算建模确定了舒尼替尼与HIF-1α的相互作用。在体外研究中，合成了舒尼替尼类似物，并在缺氧条件下评估了细胞的活力、迁移、侵袭、基质金属蛋白酶（MMPs）活性和基因表达。结果与讨论：计算分析强调了HIF-1α作为CRC转移关键介质的重要性。分子对接和动力学模拟显示，舒尼替尼及三种新型类似物与HIF-1α PAS-B结构域具有有利且稳定的相互作用。火山图显示，与其他六种CRC细胞系相比，LoVo细胞中HIF1A表达上调。体外研究结果表明，舒尼替尼及其类似物在缺氧条件下对LoVo细胞迁移和侵袭具有显著的抑制作用。明胶酶谱法和qPCR分析显示，在缺氧条件下，MMP-2和MMP-9活性降低，同时上皮-间质转化（EMT）转录因子下调。本研究报道了舒尼替尼及新型类似物对CRC细胞具有前景的抗转移作用，为对抗癌症转移的进一步研究奠定了基础。
